The 7/19-depth certificate is a reproducible, exhaustive seven-state integer computation, independently checked by direct enumeration through depth 16. Since the residue shift period divides 12, the affine map (T,H,B)->(49T,49H+32,49B-32) commutes with one-step transition, yielding an induction over all r>=7. Explicit scalar solutions and sandwich bounds give the asserted exponent and strict two-sided normalized extremal signs. Computed depths alone would not prove the infinite theorem; the induction closes the gap.

value.rationale: Exact finite-window maxima and minima are a natural extremal invariant of the classical seven-rarefied Newman sum, whereas the established literature focuses on growth and sign phenomena. The affine 49-fold renormalization with exact ±32 correction across all seven residue classes identifies a rigid discrete structure, allows explicit attained extrema for infinitely many dyadic scales, and gives sharp two-sided order of oscillation without resorting to a fractal approximation. This is a substantial characterization, not a relabeling of a known endpoint value.
